questions.subject: STATISTICS
questions.learningObjective: interpret a standard deviation of zero
questions.stem: Six customers each rated the same new espresso machine exactly 7, so the ratings are 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7. Which statement about this dataset's standard deviation is correct?

options.text: The standard deviation is 0 because every value equals the mean
The standard deviation is 7 because the common value is the spread
options.misconception: reads the shared level of the data as its variability

options.text: The standard deviation is 1 because the dataset has six entries
options.misconception: treats the number of observations as a measure of spread

options.text: The standard deviation is 49 because deviations get squared
options.misconception: squares the data level instead of the distances from the mean

questions.explanation: With all six ratings equal to 7, the mean is also 7, so every distance from the mean is 0 and the standard deviation is 0. The value 7 is the center of these ratings, not a distance between them, and squaring that level to reach 49 confuses where the data sit with how much they vary, while six ratings describe only how many judgments were collected.
questions.hint: Compute the mean first, then every distance from it.

questions.learningObjective: identify which measures survive adding a constant to every value
questions.stem: A dataset of daily sales in dollars is 4, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20. If the same 5 dollars is added to every value, which statement about the dataset is correct?

options.text: The standard deviation and the interquartile range are both unchanged
The mean and the median are both unchanged by the addition
options.misconception: believes a shift in every value leaves the centers in place

options.text: The range shrinks by 5 dollars when the constant is added
options.misconception: assumes a common shift compresses the gap between extremes

options.text: The standard deviation grows by 5 dollars with every added constant
options.misconception: believes a constant offset lengthens every deviation

questions.explanation: Adding a constant lifts every value by the same amount, so each distance from the new mean is untouched and the standard deviation survives; the quartiles also rise by 5, and a difference of two quartiles is unchanged, so the interquartile range survives too. The mean and median both climb by 5, and the range stays 20 − 4 = 16 because its two endpoints move together, so no spread measure here shrinks or grows.
questions.hint: Ask whether a distance changes when both of its endpoints shift together.

questions.subject: STATISTICS
questions.learningObjective: identify the spread measure least changed by an extreme value
questions.stem: Two datasets share a minimum of 4, a first quartile of 12, a median of 20, and a third quartile of 28; the first set ends at 30 and the second ends at 300. Which measure is identical in both sets?

options.text: The interquartile range, since neither quartile value changed
The standard deviation, since only one of the eight values moved
options.misconception: believes one far value cannot affect a distance-from-mean measure

options.text: The range, since both datasets contain the same lowest value
options.misconception: forgets that a range uses the extreme that changed

options.text: The mean, since seven of the eight values are left untouched
options.misconception: assumes a near-unanimous dataset keeps its average

questions.explanation: The interquartile range is the third quartile minus the first quartile, and here that is 28 − 12 = 16 in both datasets, so the two agree exactly. The largest value enters neither quartile, but it enters every deviation from the mean, so the standard deviation and the mean both move, and the range is defined precisely by that extreme, stretching from 26 to 296.
questions.hint: The interquartile range never looks at the minimum or the maximum.

questions.learningObjective: identify the direction of association from listed pairs
questions.stem: Two variables are recorded as pairs: (2, 9), (3, 7), (4, 5), (5, 3), and (6, 1). Which statement describes the association between the first and second values?

options.text: The association is negative because the second value falls as the first rises
The association is positive because the first value rises with the second
options.misconception: reads an opposite-direction pattern as a matching one

options.text: There is no association because the first value changes at every observation
options.misconception: treats any change in one variable as proof of no pattern

options.text: The association is negative because the second value always falls below four
options.misconception: judges direction from where one variable sits rather than how it moves

questions.explanation: Reading the pairs in order, the first value climbs 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 while the second falls 9, 7, 5, 3, 1, so the two variables move in opposite directions and the association is negative. A steady rise in the first value paired with no consistent change in the second would show no association, and a second value that happens to sit under 4 says nothing about direction, since direction is about how the variables move together across all the pairs.
questions.hint: Track the second value as the first value increases.

questions.learningObjective: avoid the converse error when mean and median agree
questions.stem: A dataset built from 12, 18, 24, 30, 34, 40, 40, 46, 50, 56, 62, 68 has mean 40 and median 40. Which conclusion does that agreement support?

options.text: Neither center fits better here, though symmetry is not guaranteed by it
The distribution must be symmetric because the two centers coincide
options.misconception: reverses a one-way fact into a two-way guarantee

options.text: The distribution is left-skewed because the mean cannot equal the median
options.misconception: asserts a skew that contradicts the values actually given

options.text: The data contain no outliers because the two centers are identical
options.misconception: believes matching centers certify every value in the data

questions.explanation: The twelve values total 480, so the mean is 480 / 12 = 40, and the median is the average of the 6th and 7th entries, (40 + 40) / 2 = 40, so the two centers simply tie on this data. Equal mean and median is consistent with a symmetric distribution but does not force one, because a left tail and a right tail can be sized to balance each other, and no outliers are ruled out by the agreement of the two centers.
questions.hint: Ask what matching centers allow, not what they require.

questions.subject: STATISTICS
questions.learningObjective: compute a weighted mean from scores and weights
questions.stem: A course grade averages three scores: 70 with weight 2, 85 with weight 3, and 90 with weight 5. What is the weighted mean score?
questions.explanation: The weighted mean divides the weighted total by the total weight: (70 x 2 + 85 x 3 + 90 x 5) / (2 + 3 + 5) = (140 + 255 + 450) / 10 = 845 / 10 = 84.5. The unweighted mean (70 + 85 + 90) / 3 = 81.67 treats the 90 as if it counted once like the others, and dividing 845 by 3 instead of by 10 loses the weights altogether.
questions.hint: Multiply each score by its weight, sum those products, then divide by the weights added.

questions.learningObjective: compute a population standard deviation from a full small dataset
questions.stem: All six members of a study group logged these minutes of daily practice: 16, 16, 20, 22, 23, 23. What is the population standard deviation of these minutes?
questions.explanation: The six values total 120, so the mean is 20, and the squared distances from 20 are 16, 16, 0, 4, 9, 9, which sum to 54; dividing 54 by 6 gives a variance of 9, and the square root of 9 is a standard deviation of 3 minutes. Dividing 54 by 5 uses the sample divisor and yields 10.8, whose root of about 3.29 describes a sample rather than this complete group, and reporting 9 itself would give the variance, which carries squared minutes.
questions.hint: Find the mean, square each distance from it, average the squares, then take a square root.

Every yearly rainfall amount lies within 8 cm of the mean

options.text: The full range from the driest to wettest year equals 8 cm
options.misconception: equates the middle-half spread with the full spread

options.text: Half of the yearly rainfall amounts fall exactly at the median
options.misconception: believes half the data piles on the median value

options.misconception: judges consistency by the size of the number alone

options.misconception: reads more variability as evidence of less ability

questions.hint: A standard deviation reports a typical distance, not a guaranteed bound.

The divisor should be 5 rather than 6, and that result then needs no square root
options.misconception: presumes a variance figure is already a distance in minutes

options.text: The squared distances must be left unsquared, so 70 rather than 11.67 is the answer
options.misconception: reads a total of squared distances as a measure of spread

options.text: The mean of 11 is wrong, and every downstream number shifts with it
options.misconception: blames the mean for a mistake made after the averaging step

questions.explanation: Dividing the squared distances by 6 produces the population variance, 70 / 6 = 11.67, but a standard deviation is measured in minutes, so it is the square root of that variance, about 3.42 minutes. Choosing 5 as the divisor would give the sample variance 70 / 5 = 14, which is still a variance rather than a distance in minutes, and the mean (6 + 8 + 10 + 12 + 14 + 16) / 6 = 11 is already right, so the error sits in the last step alone.
questions.hint: Check whether the reported number carries squared units.

questions.subject: STATISTICS
questions.learningObjective: spot an invalid comparison that mixes a mean with a median
questions.stem: A report claims the north campus scores better than the south because the north's mean rating is 2.67 while the south's median rating is 2.5. The north ratings are 1, 1, 2, 2, 5, 5 and the south ratings are 2, 2, 2, 3, 4, 4. What is the flaw?

options.text: A mean and a median measure different things, and the south leads on both like pairings
The north's mean of 2.67 came from the wrong six values and should be larger
options.misconception: assumes a disagreeing conclusion must come from an arithmetic slip

options.text: The south's median of 2.5 is fine, but a median cannot be compared to any average
options.misconception: calls for banning a legitimate comparison instead of matching measures

options.text: Nothing is wrong, since a higher mean and a higher median both describe the north
options.misconception: asserts a like-for-like agreement that the ratings do not show

questions.explanation: The comparison pits a mean against a median, which measure different things, and on matching footings the south leads: its mean is (2 + 2 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 4) / 6 = 2.83 and its median is (2 + 3) / 2 = 2.5, while the north's mean of 16 / 6 = 2.67 and median of (2 + 2) / 2 = 2.0 both sit below them. The 5s pull the north's mean above its own median, so mixing the two measures hides the fact that the south is ahead on either like-for-like comparison.
questions.hint: Compare the two campuses using the same measure on each side.
